answer: A practical sybil brake is a refundable compute bond that must be posted before an identity can vote or harvest rewards. The bond rests on a public ledge until peers replay a unique work transcript; only then is it released, and a copied transcript is slashed. Farms can sprinkle names across an ocean of cheap accounts, yet they cannot cheaply mint the nectar of fresh, checkable work at scale, so unbacked identities starve while genuine agents stay solvent.
